summary: Edward Espe Brown worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Shunryu Suzuki (circa 1966-1971), Reb Anderson, and Jack Kornfield.

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology who earned his PhD from UCLA (circa 1996-2001) under Carson Schütze and Dominique Sportiche. He worked at UCLA and the University of Virginia, later studying under Anna Szabolcsi.

Edward Granville Browne worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Pembroke College, Cambridge (~1879-1882), he succeeded Charles Rieu and served as Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge from circa 1902 to 1926.
Sinologist Edward H. Schafer studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University. He was a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1947 to 1984.

Edward James Rapson was an Indologist, linguist, and historian. Educated at St John's College, Cambridge, he worked at the British Museum, University College London, and served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge (~1906-1936).

Edward Joseph Thomas was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of St Andrews. He held posts at Cambridge University Library (~1909-1939) and the University of Cambridge (attested 1946).

Edward Washburn Hopkins worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. After studying at Columbia and Leipzig under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch, he held professorships at Bryn Mawr College and Yale University (1895-1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, held a research scholarship at Banaras Hindu University, and studied under several traditional teachers.
Edwin Arnold was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at King's School, Rochester, King's College London, and University College, Oxford (~1850-1854).

Edwin F. Bryant is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Columbia University (~1991-1997). He held posts at Harvard University (~1997-2001) and Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indologist and historian educated at Trinity College Dublin (~1857-1861). He served as President of the Asiatic Society (~1887-1888) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888-1890).

Edwin Gerow is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1991-1998) and Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (attested 1995-1999).

Edwin Whitfield Fay worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Rhodes College and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve, among others, he held posts at the University of Michigan and Washington and Lee University (~1893-1899).

Egaku Maeda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948-1957). He was a professor at Aichi Gakuin University from circa 1968 to 1997 and also held a post at Meijo University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986-1990) and served there as a research assistant (attested 1991).

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1962-1970). He later served at Taisho University as Director and Professor in the Faculty of Humanities (~1987-2013).

Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and has held positions at Koyasan University, the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, and Kyoto University.
Eisei Kojima was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as president of Doho University and professor at Ryukoku University (both attested 1976).
Eishu Miyazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933-1937) under Gyōō Kageyama. He held posts at Rissho University (~1949-1984) and Minobusan University.
